name: AWS S3
description: Protects against destructive S3 operations like bucket removal, recursive deletes, and sync --delete.

destructive_patterns.name: s3-rb
destructive_patterns.description: aws s3 rb removes an S3 bucket and is destructive.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Removing an S3 bucket deletes the bucket and optionally all objects within \ it (with --force). Bucket names are globally unique and may be claimed by \ others after deletion. Versioned objects require additional cleanup.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws s3 ls: Review bucket contents first \ - Empty the bucket before removal \ - Enable bucket versioning for recovery options

destructive_patterns.name: s3-rm
destructive_patterns.description: aws s3 rm deletes S3 objects and is destructive.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
The rm command deletes objects from S3. With --recursive, it deletes all \ objects under a prefix. For versioned buckets, this creates delete markers; \ for unversioned buckets, data is permanently lost.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws s3 ls: Review objects before deletion \ - Use --dryrun to preview what will be deleted \ - Enable versioning for recovery options

destructive_patterns.name: s3-sync-delete
destructive_patterns.description: aws s3 sync --delete removes destination objects not in source.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
The --delete flag removes files from the destination that don't exist in \ the source. This can accidentally delete important data if source and \ destination are swapped or if source is empty.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws s3 sync --dryrun: Preview changes first \ - Omit --delete for additive-only sync \ - Back up destination before syncing

destructive_patterns.name: s3api-delete-bucket
destructive_patterns.description: aws s3api delete-bucket permanently deletes a bucket.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
The delete-bucket API removes an S3 bucket. The bucket must be empty \ (including all versions and delete markers). Once deleted, the bucket \ name becomes available globally and may be claimed by others.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws s3api list-objects-v2: Verify bucket is empty \ - aws s3api list-object-versions: Check for versions \ - Use lifecycle policies for managed cleanup

destructive_patterns.name: s3api-delete-object
destructive_patterns.description: aws s3api delete-object permanently deletes an object.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an object removes it from S3. For versioned buckets, this creates \ a delete marker. Specifying a version-id permanently deletes that specific \ version. Unversioned objects are immediately and permanently deleted.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws s3api head-object: Verify object exists \ - Use bucket versioning for recovery \ - Copy to backup location before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: s3api-delete-objects
destructive_patterns.description: aws s3api delete-objects permanently deletes multiple objects.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Batch deletion removes up to 1,000 objects per request. A malformed delete \ JSON file can remove unintended objects. Deletions are processed in \ parallel and cannot be easily stopped once started.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Review the delete JSON file carefully \ - Test with a single object first \ - Enable versioning before bulk deletions
